title: Career Roadmap— B.Sc. Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning → AI Developer
summary: An AI Developer builds software applications that use artificial intelligence to solve practical problems. The role can involve integrating existing AI models, developing machine-learning pipelines, building generative AI applications, evaluating model performance, and deploying AI-powered features into production systems.

blocks.text: An AI Developer builds software applications that use artificial intelligence to solve practical problems. The role can involve integrating existing AI models, developing machine-learning pipelines, building generative AI applications, evaluating model performance, and deploying AI-powered features into production systems.

A B.Sc. in Artificial Intelligence or Machine Learning can provide a foundation for entry-level roles such as Junior AI Developer, Python Developer — AI Applications, Machine Learning Intern, or Junior Data Scientist. Employers may also expect strong programming skills, practical projects, software engineering knowledge, and, for some research-heavy roles, postgraduate qualifications.
What you will do

items.text: Build applications using Python and AI/ML libraries.
Prepare data and train or integrate machine-learning models.
Use APIs to connect AI models to web applications and business systems.
Develop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and chatbot applications where appropriate.
Evaluate accuracy, latency, reliability, and model limitations.
Deploy, monitor, test, and maintain AI-powered software.

blocks.text: Core languages
Python, SQL, basic JavaScript
Core technologies
scikit-learn, PyTorch or TensorFlow, APIs, Git
Essential strengths
Problem-solving, statistics, experimentation, debugging
Career directions
ML engineering, generative AI, data science, AI infrastructure
Start with general programming and machine-learning foundations, then select a specialization based on the kind of work you enjoy.
1. Machine Learning Developer
Builds predictive models for classification, regression, recommendations, and forecasting. Focus on statistics, data preparation, feature engineering, model evaluation, and scikit-learn.
2. Generative AI Application Developer
Integrates large language models into applications, using APIs or open models, structured outputs, tool calling, embeddings, RAG, and evaluation.
3. Computer Vision Developer
Builds systems for image classification, object detection, image processing, and video analysis. Learn OpenCV and a deep-learning framework.
4. AI Software / ML Platform Developer
Focuses on model-serving APIs, backend engineering, deployment, automated testing, data pipelines, monitoring, and reliability.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Become proficient in Python, SQL, data handling, and conventional machine learning first. Then learn deep learning and build one deployable AI application. This creates a stronger foundation than jumping between many AI frameworks or relying exclusively on prompt engineering.
This roadmap assumes a three-year B.Sc. programme. Adapt it to the actual curriculum and time remaining before graduation.
Year 1
Foundations
Develop programming and mathematical fundamentals

blocks.label: Learn Python
blocks.text: functions, classes, modules, exceptions, and file handling.

items.text: Study linear algebra, probability, statistics, and introductory calculus.
Practise data structures and algorithms, including arrays, dictionaries, stacks, queues, sorting, and searching.
Learn NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, SQL, Git, and GitHub.
Understand data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, and basic software testing.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Build two Python projects, publish readable code on GitHub, and explain your code without relying on AI-generated explanations.
Year 2
Machine learning
Learn to train and evaluate models

items.text: Study supervised and unsupervised learning, feature engineering, and model selection.
Learn regression, classification, clustering, decision trees, random forests, and gradient boosting.
Understand train/validation/test splits, cross-validation, overfitting, leakage, and evaluation metrics.
Learn neural-network fundamentals and begin using PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Build REST APIs with FastAPI or Flask and practise SQL-backed applications.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Complete a predictive ML project with a reproducible training pipeline, a baseline model, appropriate evaluation, and a clear report.
Year 3
Production AI
Build deployable AI applications

items.text: Learn a specialization such as generative AI, computer vision, NLP, or ML engineering.
Develop an API-backed AI application with validation, error handling, logging, and tests.
Learn Docker and the fundamentals of cloud deployment.
Explore embeddings, vector search, RAG, model evaluation, and responsible AI if pursuing generative AI.
Complete a capstone project, internship, or research project.
Prepare for interviews in Python, SQL, data structures, ML fundamentals, and project design.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Deploy an AI application, document its architecture and limitations, and demonstrate how you evaluate and improve its performance.
Prioritize fundamentals before advanced frameworks. You can mark your progress as you learn.

For AI Developer roles, build projects that demonstrate more than model accuracy. Employers should be able to see how you prepare data, test a solution, integrate it into software, and explain its limitations.
Project 1 — Predictive Machine Learning Application

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Beginner to intermediate
Build a classification or regression application using a public dataset. Compare a simple baseline with two or more models and choose metrics that fit the problem.

blocks.label: Suggested stack
blocks.text: Python, pandas, scikit-learn, Matplotlib, Streamlit.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Reproducible notebook, model evaluation, error analysis, and a working demo.
Project 2 — Document Question-Answering Assistant

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate
Build a RAG application that searches a controlled collection of documents and answers questions with supporting source references.

blocks.label: Suggested stack
blocks.text: Python, FastAPI, embeddings, a vector database, and an LLM.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Document ingestion, retrieval, source-linked answers, an evaluation set, and tests for unsupported questions.
Project 3 — Computer Vision Application

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate
Train or adapt an image-classification or object-detection model using a suitable public dataset. Test performance on examples that differ from the training data.

blocks.label: Suggested stack
blocks.text: Python, OpenCV, PyTorch or TensorFlow.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Working demo, evaluation results, sample predictions, and an explanation of failure cases.
Project 4 — Production-Style AI API

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Job-ready capstone
Wrap a model in a REST API. Add request validation, automated tests, logging, versioned dependencies, and deployment instructions. Measure response time and handle errors gracefully.

blocks.label: Suggested stack
blocks.text: FastAPI, scikit-learn or a model API, Docker, GitHub Actions, and a hosting platform.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Deployed demo where feasible, API documentation, tests, architecture diagram, and setup instructions.

blocks.label: Recommended capstone
blocks.text: Build an AI application that solves a clear problem for a defined audience. Include a working interface, a backend API, appropriate model evaluation, error handling, and documentation. A reliable, well-tested application is often more convincing than a collection of notebooks.
Use official documentation and build as you learn.

items.text: Python Tutorial — programming fundamentals.
NumPy and pandas — data manipulation.

blocks.text: Where to look in India

Research openings at AI product companies, software services firms, startups, analytics companies, research laboratories, and technology teams within larger organizations. Examples to investigate include TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Accenture, Microsoft, Google, and AI-focused startups. This list is for research, not confirmation of current vacancies.
Weekly job-search routine
Keep your GitHub repositories readable. Each major project should include a problem statement, setup instructions, dependencies, evaluation results, limitations, and screenshots or a demo link.

blocks.text: These are indicative stages, not guaranteed promotion timelines. Research-heavy scientist roles may require a master's degree or Ph.D., while application development roles may place greater emphasis on software engineering skills and experience.
Days 1–30
Foundations
Strengthen Python, SQL, statistics, and data manipulation. Complete a small data analysis project and practise Git and GitHub.
Days 31–60
Machine learning
Build a complete ML project, compare models, evaluate errors, and create a small interface or API. Document your results and limitations.
Days 61–90
Deployment and jobs
Deploy one application, add tests and documentation, prepare a targeted resume, practise technical interviews, and apply for internships and junior roles.
AI developer readiness tracker
I can write Python code without relying entirely on generated code.
I can use SQL and pandas to prepare data.
I understand basic ML algorithms and evaluation metrics.
I have completed at least one end-to-end AI/ML project.
I can build or integrate an API into an application.
I can explain project limitations, failure cases, and ethical considerations.
I have a clean GitHub portfolio and a targeted resume.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: For a B.Sc. AI/ML graduate in India, prioritize Python, SQL, statistics, conventional machine learning, and software engineering. Then build a deployable project in one specialization, such as generative AI, computer vision, or ML engineering. Demonstrating that you can build, test, explain, and maintain a working application is a stronger starting point than learning many frameworks superficially.
